purpose:
The report seeks approval of the
Council’s Asset Management Framework and Strategy,
establishing a corporate approach to the management,
prioritisation, review and governance of land and property assets
across the Borough. The framework supports the development of the
Corporate Landlord model and provides a structured approach to how
assets are assessed, maintained, invested in and reviewed,
supporting wider Council priorities, service delivery requirements
and financial sustainability. The report sets out the proposed
asset categorisation model, governance arrangements, investment
prioritisation principles and strategic review process that will
support future decision making across the corporate estate. It also
establishes a consistent framework for balancing operational,
financial, community and place based considerations when assessing
property related decisions. The framework is intended to strengthen
strategic oversight of the Council’s estate, improve
governance, support more coordinated asset planning and promote a
more evidence led approach to investment and estate management over
time.
content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)            
Approved the Asset Management Framework for adoption as the
council's strategic framework for the management of its property
portfolio
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Asset Management Framework as the council's strategic framework for managing its property portfolio.

purpose:
This report describes and discusses a
permanent social housing project which is a re-development of an
existing garage site. It is being developed by Housing Solutions, a
Registered Social Housing Provider. The proposal is for RBWM to
contribute capital funding to the scheme to enable the tenure to be
reduced to the social rent level (the most affordable to households
in need). The proposed capital funding will be sourced from Section
106 affordable housing receipts which RBWM received from the
developers of previous housing schemes where affordable housing was
not provided on-site. Recycling the receipts into this scheme is
advantageous in that it is possible to provide family houses
including one which is capable of adaptation for wheelchair users.
Affordable housing with these attributes is in short supply and as
a consequence this project is of some benefit to RBWM.
content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)            
Approved a capital budget along with the appropriate virements,
of £175,000, funded from Section 106 affordable housing funds
for a 4- bed house at Phipps Close, Maidenhead to enable the
delivery of the house as affordable housing with a tenure of
affordable rent capped at the Local Housing Allowance level,
payable from the Capital Programme 2026/27. This approval is
subject to Housing Solutions receipt of £55,000 from a Homes
England grant.
ii)           
Delegated authority to the Assistant Director Housing and Public
Protection in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Housing
Services, Housing Delivery and Health, for the nomination of a
suitable household to the completed property.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve funding for the construction of an affordable house in Maidenhead.

purpose:
The Council's current Corporate Cleaning
Contract is due to expire on 31 October 2026. The contract provides
cleaning services across the Council's estate, including corporate
offices, libraries, community facilities, family hubs, operational
buildings and other public-facing facilities. These services
support the delivery of safe, clean and accessible environments for
staff, elected members, service users and visitors. The current
contract was secured through the ESPO framework and is delivered by
Solo Service Group. Following engagement with Procurement the same
framework was used to secure a new contract. An expression of
interest exercise was undertaken through the framework; sufficient
supplier interest has been identified to proceed with a further
competition in accordance with the framework requirements. This
report seeks approval to delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Place, in consultation with the Cabinet Member for
Corporate Services, Transformation and Asset Management, to award
the contract to the successful bidder following completion of the
procurement process through the ESPO Total Cleaning Services
Solution Framework for the provision of corporate cleaning
services. The proposed approach will ensure compliance with
procurement legislation and the Contracts and Tendering rules,
support value for money, maintain continuity of service and provide
an efficient route to securing a future contract arrangement for
the Council's estate.
content:
That Cabinet noted
the report and:
i)            
Delegated authority to the Executive Director of Place, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Corporate Services,
Transformation and Asset Management, to award the contract to the
successful bidder following completion of the procurement process
and to enter into all necessary contractual arrangements.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to delegate authority to award a contract following completion of a procurement process

purpose:
This report will seek Cabinet approval to
participate in, and help lead, a joint Thames Valley partnership
with the Oxfordshire councils, Berkshire unitary authorities and
Swindon to progress the pre-inception phase of work for a Thames
Valley Spatial Development Strategy (SDS). The SDS is a new
strategic planning statutory requirement and is intended to provide
a high-level spatial framework setting the scale and distribution
of growth, investment opportunities and supporting Place
infrastructure across multiple local planning authority
areas.
content:
AGREED: That cabinet
noted the report and:
i)            
Approved the establishment of a partnership with the councils
covering Oxfordshire, Berkshire and Swindon to develop a statutory
Spatial Development Strategy (SDS) for the Thames Valley area as
detailed in the report.
ii)           
Noted the draft indicative funding and resource allocations for
the pre-inception programme
iii)          
Agreed that Bracknell Forest Council will act as the accountable
body for funds received/held on behalf of the partnership and will
host any staff appointed for the Thames Valley SDS
programme.
iv)          
Agreed the interim governance and oversight, monitoring and
assurance arrangements set out in this paper, including
arrangements for the period before a statutory Strategic Planning
Board (SPB) is established through secondary legislation.
v)           
Delegated the detailed agreements and working arrangements for
pre-inception development of the SDS to the Executive Director of
Place in consultation with the Deputy Director of Law &
Governance & Monitoring Officer.
vi)          
Agreed to the working arrangements for development of the
SDS.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to establish a partnership for the development of a Spatial Development Strategy in the Thames Valley area.

purpose:
The Governing Body of Riverside Primary School
has requested that the Resourced Provision at the school, for
children with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) with Speech,
Language and Communication Needs (SLNC) as a primary need, be
closed with effect from September 2026. This is because the numbers
are low, and provision no longer addresses the needs of local
pupils. Children attending the provision will continue to receive

representations received as summarised in this report and provided

is closed on 31st August 2026.
iii)            
Authorised the Executive Director of Children’s Services
and the Cabinet Member for Children’s Services, Education and
Windsor to publish a proposal to close the nursery class and to
determine the proposal following the end of the representation
period.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the closure of the Resourced Provision at Riverside Primary School and Nursery.

purpose:
This report describes a proposed social
housing project which is part of the redevelopment of the former
Heatherwood Hospital in Ascot. The new hospital was opened in 2022
in addition to 250 dwellings which are currently under construction
by Taylor Wimpey. No on-site affordable housing was deemed viable
and instead a commuted sum payment was made. Man Group has
approached RBWM offering 59 of the flats as affordable housing
which otherwise would be delivered as open market housing. Man
Group has been liaising with the RBWM Housing Service to clarify
details of the 59 flats, and to ensure that they are affordable and
meet the housing needs of households on the RBWM housing register.
The proposal is for RBWM to contribute capital funding to the
scheme to enable the tenure for all 59 flats to be social rent. The
proposed capital funding will be sourced from Section 106
affordable housing receipts which RBWM received from the developers
of previous housing schemes where affordable housing was not
provided on-site. Recycling the receipts into this scheme is
advantageous in that it is possible to provide 59 flats as
affordable housing on a site in Ascot which otherwise would have no
affordable housing, and is therefore of significant benefit to
RBWM.
content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)                
Recommended that Council approved a capital budget of
£3,400,000, funded from Section 106 affordable housing funds
for 59 flats at Heatherwood Royal, Ascot to enable the delivery of
the flats as affordable housing with a tenure of social rent,
payable from the Capital Programme 2026/27. And subject to receipt
of £8.56m Homes England grant to Man Group.
ii)              
Delegated authority to the Assistant Director Housing and Public
Protection in consultation with the Cabinet Member for Housing
Services, Housing Delivery and Health, for the operational delivery
of the homes and nomination of suitable households to the completed
properties.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a capital budget for the construction of affordable housing flats at Heatherwood Royal, Ascot.

content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)                
Considered the recommendations made by Corporate Overview &
Scrutiny at their meeting on 18 March 2026, and agreed to accept
the following:

·       
Reviewing the wording in the Council Plan foreword from the
Leader of the Council, where reference was made to ‘a strong
financial footing’.

·       
Publish a version of the plan which outlined the various
amendments which had been made, so it was clear to Councillors and
residents what had changed in the refresh.

·       
Publish a list of targets or deliverables that had been removed
from the Council Plan with a reason why these had been
removed.

·       
Explore the adoption of a version control policy for any reports
which would be considered by Councillors across all council
meetings, to improve the process.

·       
Consider whether the Council Plan was both achievable and
adaptable to the current resourcing level across the
council.

·       
Add a reference to the Corporate Social Responsibility Social
Value Policy, if this was to be created.

·       
Strengthen objective 1.6 in the Council Plan to consider how a
KPI or measure of success could be incorporated. This could also be
linked to a metric on the amount of asset space not currently being
utilised.

·       
Consider attaching a deliverable to aim 1.1 around improvements
to scrutiny, forecasting and monitoring of the council’s
budget.

·       
Explore adding more tangible external outcomes where residents
would notice a positive difference.
ii)              
Agreed to take the Council Plan to Council in April for
consideration and agreement.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for reviewing and amending the Council Plan, including changes to wording and exploring version control policies.

AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)                
Noted the Chief Financial Officer’s section 25 statement
set out in Section 11 of the report.
ii)              
Recommended that Council approved the 2026/27 budget,
specifically the:
a) net revenue budget of
£185.152m as set out in the main body of this report;
b) fees and charges as set
out in Appendix E;
c) Capital and Treasury
strategy, including the Minimum Revenue Provision policy as set out
in Appendix F;
d) capital programme as
set out on Appendix G;
e) the pay policy set out
in Appendix J; and
f) pay award of
£2,000 per full time equivalent post, from 1 April 2026 for
all staff paid on RBWM local pay scales as set out in Appendix J to
this report.
iii)            
Recommended that Council approved:
a) the schools budget in line with Appendix I of this
report;
b) the proposals for the
Schools Block (Appendix I, para 5.4), Schools Funding Formula
(Appendix I, Annex A) and Schools Allocations (Appendix I, Annex B)
including a Minimum Funding Guarantee of 0% per pupil;
c) the proposals outlined
in the Central School Services Block (Appendix I, para
5.11);
d) the proposals outlined
for the Early Years Block (Appendix I, para 5.12); and
e) the proposals outlines
for the High Needs Block (Appendix I, para 5.19).
iv)            
Recommended that Council approved the flexible use of capital
receipts strategy set out in Appendix H to fund transformation
related spend of up to £3.313m in 2025/26, and delegates
authority to the Executive Director of Resources to authorise any
further schemes up to £0.500m, in 2026/27 in line with the
strategy (paragraph 7 and Appendix H).
v)              
Recommended that Council approved the calculations for
determining the Council Tax requirement for 2026/27 as set out in
Appendix O, consisting of:
a) a Council Tax
requirement of £110,250,779;
b) a Band D charge of
£1,504.41 for the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead in
2026/27, reflecting an overall increase of 7.49% based on:
- a £76.84 (5.49%)
increase in base Council Tax taking the charge to £1,263.90
for 2026/27; and
- an additional
£27.99 to reflect an increase in the Adult Social Care
Precept with is proposed as £240.51,
c) the Special Expenses
Precept increases by £2.99 (7.48%) to £42.94 for
2026/27 for the unparished areas of Windsor and Maidenhead in
accordance with Section 35 of the Local Government Finance Act
19992, as set out in Appendix O, Table O3.
vi)            
Noted the following precepts by partner organisations:
a) The Police and Crime
Commissioner for the Thames Valley, £298.28, as set out in
appendix O, Table O2.
b) Royal Berkshire Fire
Authority, £91.31, as set out in appendix O,
Table O2.
c) Parish precepts as set
out in Appendix O, Table O2, as notified
by the individual
parishes.

purpose:
To provide clarity to customers on the
National Validation Requirements that are currently in place, and
to introduce new Local Validation Requirements permitted by current
legislation. All our neighbouring local planning authorities,
together with most local authorities across the country have
published Local Validation Requirements. The introduction of Local
Validation Requirements sets out the information and documentation
required to make a planning application valid, i.e. live. This
means that Officers will have all the information needed to
determine an application. Currently a notable number of
applications have to be refused on insufficient information and
whilst we ask for the additional information where possible, this
is often not possible within the statutory timescales. The
introduction of the Local Validation Requirements will not only
ensure RBWM is on a par with other LPAs, but also provide clarity
and guidance for our applicants. This should, in turn, lead to
fewer refusals, fewer appeals, more approvals and greater customer
satisfaction
content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
i)                
Approved the adoption of the National and Local Validation
Requirements and its implementation on 24th February 2026.
ii)              
Delegated authority to the Assistant Director of Planning in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Planning, to approve and
publish any minor changes to the National and Local Validation
Requirements, prior to its publication.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the adoption and implementation of National and Local Validation Requirements

purpose:
This report recommends that the Cabinet adopts
the Maidenhead Town Centre Shopfront Supplementary Planning
Document (SPD). The SPD provides detailed guidance for new and
replacement shopfronts within the Maidenhead Town Centre Strategic
Placemaking Area, as defined in Policy QP1a of the Borough Local
Plan. The document reframes and updates much of the guidance from
the existing ‘Maidenhead Business & Shop Front Design
Guide’, dated August 2013. This SPD is a more visual and
accessible document than the existing guidance, providing quick
guides and checklists for applicants, retailers, developers and
planning officers. The SPD will help to advance the strategic aims
and priorities of the Council Plan 2024-28. In particular, it will
assist with the Strategic priority to “Develop a more
coherent approach to regeneration and place-making across the
borough’s key locations, and ensure economic and housing
development benefits local communities.”
content:

consultation with the Cabinet Member for Adult Services, Planning
& Governance for minor changes to be made to the Maidenhead
Town Centre Shopfront Supplementary Planning Document prior to
publication.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to adopt the Maidenhead Town Centre Shopfront Supplementary Planning Document.

content:
AGREED: That Cabinet
noted the report and:
 
i)            
Endorsed the benefits from the proposed devolution of powers and
functions set out in the English Devolution and Community
Empowerment Bill.
 
ii)           
Recommended to Full Council (17 December 2025) that it approved
the joint Expression of Interest (EOI) attached at Appendix B be
submitted to the Secretary of State, noting that the EOI was
designed to proactively position the region for early consideration
in the next wave of the devolution programme.
 
iii)          
Acknowledged the EOI as an invitation to government to open
dialogue and engagement with the region regarding the potential
form and operation of a Mayoral Strategic Authority, and not a
decision to establish an MSA.
 
iv)          
Agreed that further update reports be brought back to Cabinet
and Full Council as necessary and prior to any final decision to
create an MSA.
 
v)           
Noted that an informal Devolution Board – comprised of
council Leaders - will oversee discussions with government,
ensuring robust governance and stakeholder engagement by elected
members throughout this process.
topline: The Council has decided to endorse the benefits of devolution and recommend the submission of an Expression of Interest for potential establishment of a Mayoral Strategic Authority.
